differences.what: massing: the narrow brick front under its steep street hip, the long north flank running back past the round tower to the coped gables of the ranges and the garage, the two very tall stacks and the street dormers stand where the plate draws them, the stacks' tops, the tower's top and the hip's finial within about 10-30 px through this view's camera (fitted to them and the fence's foot)

the near stack's place: the plate stands it about 28 px (about 1.4 m) closer to the tower than the record does, as the 1919 programme plate's camera also finds (23 px) and the 1913 plate's does not; two of three plates against one, on stacks the cameras are fitted to, is a gap the fits disagree about

the third, smaller gable the plates draw at the flank's far end, coped and finialled as the ranges' are: T-3354 roofs the garage under a slated gable facing the flank, pitched 54 degrees to an apex at 15.7 m, with the ranges' stone coping, kneelers and 0.6 m finial (where it was flat in tin); through this camera its apex lands on the plate's third gable within about 15 px

the steep gables over the rear ranges, coped and finialled (T-3337), stand where the plate's two nearer gables do in kind and count; the small pinnacled dormers between the gables, on the slope the plates show facing the street: all three plates draw two, standing between the rear range's gable and the middle range's over the flank's flat-topped bays; through the 1919 and 1912 cameras they fall where the rear range's street-facing slope stands over its north end (about u -7.5, v -4.5 to -3.3), which the record's ranges leave about 1.7 m of before the middle range's roof meets it. Not built: K01 builds dormers on a hip's slopes and the front, not on a rear wing's gable roof, and their place waits on the ranges' plan (above)

the rear ranges' gables against all three Gatlin plates (T-3354): through the 1912, 1913 and 1919 plates' cameras the garage's new north gable lands on the plates' third gable within about 15 px, but the two ranges' gables do not: the rear range's apex stands about 20-35 px (about 1-2 m) left of the plates' and the middle range's about 25-30 px left and 30-60 px (about 2-3 m) under them, the same way in all three. The three cameras are fitted to the front block alone and agree with one another; moving the 1912 camera's eye back along its degenerate line (u 47 to 90) moves the ranges' gables further from the plate's, not nearer. So the difference is the ranges', not a fit's: the plates stand the middle range's gable nearer the street and much higher than the 1911 sheet's trace (u -7 to 0) and a 50-degree gable over its 7 m span can reach (13.8 m; K01 slates nothing over 60 degrees). Not rebuilt here: the sheet's plan is the trace the house stands on, and the plates do not show the ranges' plan, so re-cutting it waits on a reading that reconciles the two (L-k01-1919-garage-gable-3354)

the north flank's two-storey flat-topped bays and their mullioned windows: the plate draws the flank's lower storeys in deep shade behind the parkway trees; it confirms a flat-topped two-storey block under the far gables and pale corners at the ranges' steps, as the 1919 plate does, but resolves no window, no balustrade and none of the canted bay's own corners; the quoined flat-topped block at the middle range's north-west corner the 1919 plate shows is not built

the street dormers: the broad three-light dormer and the small one-light dormer beside it, with the stack rising behind them at the front block's south side (T-3280, T-3301), stand over the plate's within about 30 px
the round tower's flat top under its heavy edge (T-3280), standing between the two tall stacks as the plate draws it
the front's lower storeys, the bow, the stoop and the entrance: the parkway trees and the hedge behind the fence hide them
the south neighbour (1923, the mansard at the plate's right edge), the parkway trees, the lamp post and the fence's pattern: not part of this record
